      ORDER DEFINING SECOND NOTICE AND SOCIAL MEDIA CAMPAIGN

       THIS MATTER comes before the Hearing Examiners upon El Paso Electric Company’s

(“EPE”) Response to Order on EPE’s Proposed Second Notice and Social Media Campaign

(“EPE’s Response”). Being duly informed, the Hearing Examiners FIND and CONCLUDE:

       1.       On August 27, 2026, the Hearing Examiners issued their Order Establishing

Revised Procedural Schedule and Addressing Outstanding Motions (“August 27th Order”), in

which the Hearing Examiners ordered EPE to file a proposed form of website notice for EPE’s

Amended Application, and to describe the manner in which EPE will conduct a social media

campaign for that notice, including a description of how the social media campaign will connect

customers to the form of notice that will be made available on EPE’s website. The Hearing

Examiners also ordered that on or before September 10, 2026, parties were permitted to file

comments on EPE’s proposed form of website notice and EPE’s filed plan for its social media

campaign. Further, the Hearing Examiners committed to confirming and/or defining the final form

of website notice, and social media campaign, on or before September 15, 2026.

       2.       On September 3, 2026, EPE filed its Notice of Compliance Filing of Proposed

Form of Website Notice (“EPE’s Compliance Filing”).

       3.       On September 10, 2026, the City of Las Cruces (“CLC”) filed CLC’s Comments

on EPE’s Proposed Second Notice to EPE Customers and Social Media Campaign (“CLC’s

Comments”).
             BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION
Order Defining Second Notice and Social Media Campaign Docket No. 25-00082-UT


          4.        On September 15, 2026, the Hearing Examiners issued the Order on EPE’s

Proposed Second Notice and Social Media Campaign (“Sept. 15th Order”), which identified that

EPE’s Compliance Filing had not provided a complete table of rates for all rate classes,1 that it is

reasonable that a second notice to EPE customers should provide access to information for all rate

classes,2 and that EPE had not provided sufficient information for the Hearing Examiners to be

able to confirm or define EPE’s filed plan for its social media campaign.3

          5.        The Sept. 15th Order therefore ordered EPE to make a filing by September 18,

2026, that included a complete table of rates, and a comparison of present and proposed rates for

each customer class as requested in EPE’s Amended Application, as well as a description of the

actual text that EPE’s “advertisement” would utilize in its social media campaign, and a more

robust explanation of the amount of communications that will be disseminated in the social media

campaign.4

          6.        On September 18, 2026, EPE filed EPE’s Response.

          7.        EPE’s Response includes Attachment A, which is a complete table of rates

showing a Residential Typical Bill Comparison of EPE’s phase-in proposal, as requested in EPE’s

Amended Application, in the format required by the Sept. 15th Order.

         8.         EPE’s Response includes Attachment B, which is a comparison of present and

proposed rates for each customer class, as requested in EPE’s Amended Application, in the format

required by the Sept. 15th Order.

         9.         EPE’s Response includes Attachment C, which includes a description of the

actual text that EPE’s advertisement will utilize to communicate with users of the Meta platforms,

and provides that text in the form of an image that represents the visual display that users of the

Meta platforms will see.5

         10.        Attachment C to EPE’s Response also includes an explanation of the amount of

communications that will be disseminated in the social media campaign. It proposes that the

campaign be run from September 28, 2026 through October 19, 2026, lists the zip codes to which

the campaign will be targeted, explains how the campaign will also utilize relevant professional

and interest -based targeting criteria, provides the times of day during which the campaign will be

run, and provides statistics regarding impressions and link clicks that were generated by a previous

campaign that used the same outreach methodology.6

         11.        EPE’s Response provides the information required by the Sept. 15th Order, and

provides sufficient information to understand the methodologies that EPE will implement in order

to provide notice of its Amended Application through a social media campaign. The proposed text

and imagery provides a clear “Notice to EL Paso Electric New Mexico Customers” and a sufficient

communication that such notice is given so that those customers can “Learn more about our

amended application to revise retail rates.” Further, it is explained that “[t]he advertisement will

         12.        EPE’s Response, in sum, provides sufficient information for the Hearing

provide notice of EPE’s Amended Application.

         13.        Further, EPE’s plan provides a reasonable methodology for providing notice of

the Amended Application, as EPE previously provided notice of its originally filed notification

through bill stuffers, newspaper publication, and social media.7

         14.        The proposed dates for the social media campaign run from September 28 through

should end prior to the intervention deadline, so the social media campaign should be shortened

and may reduce costs.

                SECOND NOTICE TO EPE CUSTOMERS

This Second Notice relates to El Paso Electric Company’s (“EPE”) Application with the New
Mexico Public Regulation Commission, requesting approval of revised New Mexico retail
electric base rates and is provided to inform EPE’s customers of changes to the Application
and the date of public hearing. On July 16, 2026, the New Mexico Public Regulation
Commission ordered EPE to file an Amended Application and replacement filing package
reflecting the impact of corrections identified in the course of proceedings to the revenue
requirement and rate calculations. EPE filed the Amended Application on August 6, 2026,
stating that the non-fuel base rate revenue deficiency shown in EPE’s proposed cost of
service changed from $70.6 to $70.7 million and now demonstrates the need for a 50.5%
base rate increase, which is offset by a $0.2 million reduction in miscellaneous service
revenue, for a net operating revenue increase of $70.5 million in these New Mexico
revenues. EPE’s Amended Application does not change its request for an 8.35% weighted
cost of capital, a return on equity of 10.7% and an equity to debt capital structure of 55.5%
and 45.5%. According to EPE, the increase is required to recover costs for EPE’s $408.44
million investment since its 2020 rate case, including investments in distribution,
transmission, nuclear production, local generating plants and general plant. EPE is also
proposing to include in base rates its Commission approved advanced metering system
(“AMS”), and the annual capacity costs associated with Commission approved agreements
for three battery energy storage facilities.

NO ACTION IS REQUIRED ON YOUR PART UNLESS YOU WANT TO BECOME
            A PARTY OR COMMENT ON THE APPLICATION
EPE’s previously noticed revised rates, set forth in Advice Notice No. 317, represent the
maximum rates that can be approved in this proceeding. Where the rates provided in the
Amended Application exceed the rates that were set forth in Advice Notice No. 317, the
rates in Advice Notice No. 317 will be the ceiling for rates that may be approved by the
 Commission at the conclusion of the proceedings in Docket No. 25-00082-UT, that are
described below. If approved, the revisions will affect all retail classifications.

To moderate the rate impact on certain customer classes, EPE has proposed to voluntarily
phase in recovery through a two-part implementation process for base rates for Rate Nos.
01 (Residential), 05 (Irrigation), 10B (Military), 12 (Private Lighting), 25 (Outdoor Lighting), and
26 (State University). EPE has proposed that the first phase, expected to take effect on April
15, 2027, represents a system average increase of 26.8% for these rate classes; and the
second phase, proposed to take effect on October 1, 2027, reflects an additional 18.7%
increase relative to Phase 1.

EPE states that the bill impact of the Amended Application base rate changes will be
partially offset by an anticipated reduction in Renewable Portfolio Standard (“RPS”) costs.
The proposed increases will be to both the customer charge and the energy charge rates.
For example, EPE projects that a residential customer using an average of 750 kWh during a
summer month, would have a combined impact of a bill increase of 22.5% in Phase 1
followed by an additional increase of 28.3% in Phase 2, effectively totaling 57.2%. For that
residential customer, EPE’s proposed increase in non-fuel base rates represents a bill
increase of $24.65 in Phase 1 followed by an additional bill increase of $30.46 per summer
month in Phase 2, totaling $55.11. The combined impact of the proposed base rate changes
and the RPS cost reduction for a residential customer using an average of 500 kWh during a
winter month will be a bill increase of 14.7% in Phase 1 followed by an additional bill
increase of 28.7% in Phase 2, effectively totaling 47.7%. For that residential customer, EPE’s
proposed increase in non-fuel base rates represents a bill increase of $10.95 in Phase 1
followed by an additional bill increase of $17.21 per winter month in Phase 2, totaling
$28.16.

EPE is also proposing to implement customer rate options that include: (i) a new Low-
Income Rider to qualified households in the Residential Service Rate that credits the
customer charge dollar for dollar; (ii) experimental off-peak and time-of-day (“TOD”)
demand rates designed to further incentivize certain commercial customers to shift load
   from peak hours; (iii) and a new two-year Peak Time Rebate Pilot Program intended to
  incentivize Residential Service Rate customers to shift to off-peak usage times by providing
  pilot participants the opportunity to receive a bill credit for reducing energy consumption
  during peak periods following a notification from EPE. EPE has also proposed new Large
  Load Tariff Schedules Rates No. 50 and 51.

  Additionally, EPE asks the Commission to:

  1. Authorize several design changes to (i) align recovery of demand energy and customer
     costs with how those costs are incurred, thereby minimizing intra-class subsidization,
     (ii) provide customers with accurate price signals that convey cost differences between
     seasonal and non-seasonal time periods to encourage energy conservation and
     potentially reduce customer contribution to EPE’s system peak, (iii) promote stability,
     and (iv) allow EPE the opportunity to recover the costs of providing safe and reliable
     service.
  2. Authorize the proposed replacement of its Rule No. 8 Line Extension Policy and related
     revisions to its Rule 13 Increase or Decrease of Connected Load.
  3. Authorize the inclusion in base rates of the capacity costs already incurred under the
     Commission-approved Buena Vista 1 Power Purchase Agreement since that resource
     came online in 2023.

  customer class under Advice Notice No. 317 proposed by EPE. The other customer class
  rate tables and a comparison of present and proposed rates for each customer class, are
  presented in Attachments A and B at the end of this document. These rate comparisons are
  for informational purposes only and the final rate design may vary the final rates ultimately
  charged to each class and for each consumption level.

                                   PUBLIC HEARING
A public hearing to hear and receive testimony and exhibits is set for December 9 through
22, 2026, commencing at 9:00 a.m. each day. The hearing will be conducted online and
can be viewed via livestream on the Commission’s YouTube channel and its website,
https://www.prc.nm.gov/public-hearings/. Please contact the Commission for
confirmation of the hearing, because hearings are occasionally cancelled or rescheduled.

                                  PUBLIC COMMENT
People who are not associated with a party to this case may make written or oral
comment, without becoming an intervenor, as allowed by Rule 1.2.2.23(F) NMAC.
Written or oral comment will not be considered as evidence in the proceeding.

Written comments must refer to Docket Number 25-00082-UT and be submitted before the
Commission makes a final decision. Written comments and any other filings should be
submitted online through PRCe360 Docketing System. Comments can also be sent via US
mail to PRC Records P.O. Box 1269, Santa Fe, NM 87504.

Alternatively, oral public comment is also welcome during Commission open meetings. The
open meeting schedule can be found at www.prc.nm.gov/nmprc-open-meeting-agenda/.
Email public.comment@prc.nm.gov or call (505) 490-7910 to sign up to comment online or
 by phone at an open meeting. If the Commission determines a separate hearing should be
set for oral comments for this matter, the date, time, and location will be announced on the
Commission’s website, https://www.prc.nm.gov/.

Instructions to submit written public comment online, to file pleadings and other
documents,       and     to     view       Commission         dockets        are    found      at
https://e360.prc.nm.gov/portal/public/#/public/nm-prc/en/home. All filings subject to
deadlines must be submitted within regular business hours of the due date to be considered timely
filed.

                                  TO BECOME A PARTY
If you wish to appear in this case as a party, you must file a motion for leave to intervene,
pursuant to 1.2.2.23 NMAC, on or before October 16, 2026. Intervenors must become
familiar with the rules regarding practicing before the Commission and all other applicable
rules.

The Commission’s Rules of Procedure 1.2.2 NMAC apply except as modified by order of the
Commission or Hearing Examiners. These and other rules are available online at
https://srca.nm.gov/nmac-home/nmac-titles/.
